title: On Representation Smoothness for Robust Architecture Discovery of Variational Quantum Circuits

problem.claim: Discovering diverse, high-performing structured models in mixed discrete–continuous search spaces requires stable and effective representations of candidate models.

gap.claim: Existing VQC encodings enable evolutionary discovery but introduce representational discontinuities that degrade search stability and robustness.

contributions.claim: Introduces a smooth, continuous mechanism for gate selection.
Introduces a factorized representation separating structural discovery from continuous parameter optimization.
Finds encoding smoothness to be an important principle for robust discovery in structured model spaces.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across multiple circuit discovery tasks, combining both encoding suggestions produced smoother representations, higher-quality exploration, and lower volatility of discovered models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Structured model discovery in mixed discrete–continuous spaces is a recurring challenge.
Representation choice affects search stability and effectiveness, particularly for VQCs with discrete architectural choices and continuous parameters.
Existing encodings create discontinuities that weaken search stability and robustness.
The paper proposes smooth gate selection and a factorized representation.
The combined refinements reportedly improve representation smoothness and exploration outcomes while reducing model volatility.

source_observation.claim: Encoding discontinuities are associated with reduced search stability and robustness.

interpretation.claim: In structured search, representation geometry may materially shape optimization behavior.

application.claim: Evaluate and, where possible, smooth representation changes when designing discovery systems over structured model spaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that smooth representations are beneficial for all structured search settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the circuit discovery tasks, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe implementation details or evaluation conditions.
